item.title: Careless dismissals give Australia route to series win
item.description: The winner of the third Test will finish the series top of the International Cricket Council's Test rankings [Getty Images] Third Test, Cape Town (day three of five) South Africa 329 & 140-4: Ackerman 62; Starc 2-29 Australia 429: Inglis 102; Harmer 4-104 South Africa lead by 40 runs Scorecard Batters carelessly gifting wickets to Australia... we have been here before. This time it was not England helping their opponents, although they will have taken note with a tour of South Africa to come this winter. South Africa's attempt to fight back in the decisive third Test against Australia was hurt by two poor strokes on day three. Having taken the last six Australian wickets for 99 runs in the morning despite Josh Inglis' second Test century, the Proteas began their second innings facing a deficit of exactly 100. They needed runs from their experienced opener and number three. Neither Aiden Markram nor David Bedingham could deliver. By the end, even captain Temba Bavuma had been tempted into a wild swipe to fall for 35. South Africa were 140-4, just 40 runs ahead, at the close. Australia are closing in. Weakness exposed by Australia In isolation, Markram's drive off Mitchell Starc straight into the hands of mid-off for one appeared the most egregious. The ball was the fullest of the six balls Markram faced but not there for him to play his trademark shot. Fielder Travis Head did not have to move. Worse, though, was the dismissal of Bedingham, who showed he had not learned from the first innings. Then, the right-hander top-edged a pull to Josh Hazlewood off the bowling of Starc. This time he repeated the shot, with Hazlewood the wicket-taking bowler. "That is just absolutely soft from David Bedingham," said former South Africa bowler Vernon Philander. "He knew they were going to target him in that zone. For the second time in the Test, he has fallen to the same ploy." The delivery which dismissed Markram was the fullest he had faced but still not full enough to be a driving length [CricViz] Given the prized position in South Africa's batting order on the back of strong domestic form for Durham in the County Championship and twin hundreds for Western Province in September, this score of 11 followed contributions of 49, 46 and 50 in his other four innings. He has got in but has not made a match-winning contribution. Batting in the key position of first drop, some would say that is more infuriating than not getting in at all. His dismissal, again like in the first innings, came shortly after being hit by a bouncer, with Starc clattering one into his chest on this occasion. When, after starting with two balls on a good length, Hazlewood went short again, Bedingham's eyes lit up. Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer and co should have been taking note. It was the fifth time he has been dismissed pulling in his 18 Tests. On average he gets out playing that shot once every 13 deliveries. item.title: College football's traditions are for sale. Florida-Georgia shows the multi-million-dollar price tag
item.description: College football in the 2020s is a never-ending war between commerce and tradition, between a deep desire to preserve universities’ distinctive identities and an even deeper desire to make money off those distinctive identities. One of the war’s most notable battles is unfolding on the shores of the Atlantic Ocean in Jacksonville, Florida, where two of the SEC’s rivals meet every year in a celebrated, anticipated, cherished battle. (Well, not every year, but we’ll get to that.) Florida-Georgia — or Georgia-Florida, depending on whether you’re wearing red or blue to the game — is one of only three standing rivalry games played at a neutral site every year. (Texas-Oklahoma and Army-Navy are the others.) It’s achieved legendary status for both institutions; a pilgrimage to Jacksonville is a must for every Dawg and Gator. “It's one of the few events where twice as many people come to experience the game than actually go into the game,” says Michael Corrigan, president and CEO of Visit Jacksonville. “The stadium holds some 80,000 people. Well, there's 150,000 people that are tailgating or participating some way in that particular weekend. … It’s a three-and-a-half to four-hour commercial about Jacksonville, Florida on national TV.” “Jacksonville being a border town, there's just a lot of history and tradition,” Florida athletic director Scott Stricklin told Yahoo Sports. “It just holds a unique place in college football lore, and it's important for our school to maintain that part of the rivalry.” It’s a fantastic tradition, yes, but it’s also immensely lucrative, and as we’ve seen everywhere across the college football landscape, tradition doesn’t stand a chance against money. And what happens next in the Georgia-Florida-Jacksonville equation — which now includes Atlanta and Tampa for the next two years — could herald changes ahead for other major programs across the country. A general view of tailgating areas outside the stadium before the game between the Florida Gators and the Georgia Bulldogs on November 1, 2025 at EverBank Field in Jacksonville. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The World’s Largest Outdoor Branding Opportunity Corporate and brand-minded interests have dubbed this year’s Florida-Georgia game the “Invesco QQQ Atlanta Gridiron Classic,” but everyone involved knows it by its traditional name: the World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party. When you’re a student, you hang wherever you can find a beer and a bed; Frat Beach in nearby St. Simons Island is a longstanding Georgia tradition. When you’re an alum with a bit more disposable income, you rent a Duval County Airbnb and whip up themed cocktails. And everyone, young and old, descends on Jacksonville’s EverBank Stadium, dividing neatly into “Georgia” and “Florida” quadrants. Well, except this year and next. item.title: Cowboys RB Javonte Williams considered retirement before signing with team
item.description: Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams has revealed that he nearly walked away from the NFL before finding a new lease on his football career in Dallas. The 26-year-old admitted that his time with the Denver Broncos left him questioning his future in the sport before joining the Cowboys and rediscovering his passion for the game. Speaking on Down 2 Business on Wednesday, Williams opened up about how close he came to retiring and explained how his move to Dallas completely changed his outlook. Dallas Cowboys RB Javonte Williams said on @downs2business that following his time with the Denver Broncos and before signing with the Cowboys he gave thought to retiring, just with everything that had happened in his career at that point. "I was really about to just hang up the cleats." "No disrespect to nobody in Denver or nothing like that, I respect everybody over there, I respect what they got going on… just coming to Dallas it felt like it’s a new awakening. I felt like a rebirth." "Just leaving there and coming here, the coaches believing in me, everybody just like lifting me up. It kind of felt like UNC all over again. Me just going out there just playing, having fun." "I just fell in love with the game again. I really had lost love for the game… I had already bought a crib… I’m like I might just start my real estate or something." Javonte gave credit to his faith and family for helping him give things another go. — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) October 28, 2026 “I was really about to just hang up the cleats,” Williams said. “No disrespect to anybody in Denver… just coming to Dallas it felt like it’s a new awakening.” Williams also revealed that he had “lost love for the game” and had apparently considered pursuing a career in real estate instead. item.title: Anthony Joshua coach reacts to Tyson Fury’s ‘traitor’ jibe based on shared history
item.description: Ben Davison has played down Tyson Fury ’s “tongue-in-cheek” claim that the coach is a “traitor”, after Davison reunited with Anthony Joshua ahead of a fight with the “Gypsy King”. Davison coached Fury in 2018, when the heavyweight returned to boxing after a two-year hiatus, guiding his fellow Briton to wins over Francesco Pianeta and Sefer Seferi before a draw with Deontay Wilder – in a fight that most fans felt Fury had won. Fury remained with Davison for victories over Tom Schwarz and Otto Wallin, but he split from the coach ahead of a 2020 rematch with Wilder, which Fury won via stoppage – before repeating that result in 2021. Tyson Fury (left) and his former trainer Ben Davison before their split (PA) Davison then partnered with Joshua in 2023, leading “AJ” to knockouts of Wallin and Francis Ngannou, but the pair parted ways after a stoppage loss to Daniel Dubois in 2024. Joshua has fought twice since, stopping YouTuber Jake Paul in December and Kristian Prenga in July, and now he has reunited with Davison ahead of a long-awaited super-fight with Fury . Fury vs Joshua will take place on 11 December, as the former world heavyweight champions headline at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, and backstage at a press conference to promote that bout, Fury playfully labelled Davison a “traitor”. “I think it’s tongue in cheek,” Davison told Playbook Boxing , powered by Betway . “I’ll be honest, I don’t think he cares who works with AJ. But I think most importantly, I spent a lot of time with him, and I think deep down he knows what type of person I am. “I think he would say: ‘I know Ben’s a good guy.’ He’s smart enough to understand that boxing is a business, and hopefully he feels the same way I do, where it doesn’t have an impact. Like I say, he could say whatever it is that he wanted to – call me this, call me that, whatever; it wouldn’t change how things are, because deep down I have the same, where I know he’s a good guy. “Of course it’s a little bit awkward, [but] I’ve got a lot of love and a lot of respect for Tyson [...] It’s solely business. He can say whatever he wanted to say. He could call me ‘rotten’ if he wanted to. Davison checking on Anthony Joshua after the latter’s KO by Daniel Dubois (Getty) “I never fell out with any ex-fighters that I’ve worked with, and it’s important to me that stays the same. But at the same time, I’ve got a fantastic relationship and a lot of love for AJ as well.” As Davison, 33, prepares to coach Joshua against Fury, the trainer has actually played down the significance of his past with the Gypsy King. Saying there is “not really” a conflict of interest, Davison explained: “I think Tyson’s developed as a fighter. There’s nothing that I would know about him that you couldn’t see by watching one of his fights, in terms of boxing. “Outside of that, I think that’s something that AJ respects: I never go to AJ and talk to him about Tyson. item.title: Maryland offers buy-one, get-two-free tickets ahead of Illinois matchup
item.description: Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; The Maryland Terrapins warm up before a game against the UCLA Bruins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Maryland is pulling out all the stops to pack SECU Stadium ahead of Saturday’s matchup against Illinois, including a ticket promotion that gives fans two free tickets with the purchase of one. The Terrapins announced the Halloween promotion Monday, giving fans the unique opportunity to buy three tickets for the price of one. Thus, the orange and blue may have a tougher task in College Park than they originally planned. The unusual promotion comes amid a disastrous season for Maryland, which sits at 2-5 overall and 0-4 in Big Ten play. The Terrapins recently fired head coach Mike Locksley following their 12th consecutive conference loss. Maryland is also offering students the chance to win free tuition for the spring semester if they attend Saturday’s game and remain through the fourth quarter. Maryland only averaged just over 40,000 fans in 2025, ranking near the bottom of the Big Ten in attendance. With interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim making his debut, Maryland is hoping discounted tickets and a tuition giveaway will help create a home-field advantage against the Illini.

item.title: As Houston Astros look to fill needs, here are MLB's 20 best free agents this offseason
item.description: Tarik Skubal (left), Jazz Chisholm (center) and Randy Arozarena (right) are some of the top free agents in baseball for the 2026-27 offseason. (Getty Images) The Milwaukee Brewers capped off a dominant season in fitting fashion, capturing the franchise's first World Series on Wednesday after winning 103 games in the regular season, then going 11-2 in the postseason. Now, the rest of baseball will try to catch them. Baseball free agency has started with players able to sign with new teams as soon as 4 p.m. Monday. It could be a tight window, because Major League Baseball's collective bargaining agreement expires at midnight on Dec. 1 , which could lead to a long lockout. However, when this happened in 2021, there was a flurry of free agent activity before the CBA expired, including the Texas Rangers signing both Corey Seager and Marcus Semien to huge deals. The Astros, who have a few key players of their own hitting free agency , have holes to fill, particularly in the outfield and starting rotation. Here's how we rank the 20 best free agents to hit the open market this offseason… 1. Tarik Skubal, starting pitcher, Dodgers Tarik Skubal of the Los Angeles Dodgers looks on from the dugout prior to Game Four of the National League Championship Series between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Los Angeles Dodgers at UNIQLO Field at Dodger Stadium on Thursday, October 15, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) It can't even be debated who the top prize on the free agent market is this offseason. The only question is just how much money is he going to get. The two-time Cy Young Award winner turns 30 in November, meaning whoever signs him is getting an ace in his prime. If the Phillies gave Zack Wheeler $42 million per year and the Tigers gave Framber Valdez $38.3 million per year , then Skubal's got to get at least $50 million a year, right? 2. item.title: Arsenal could be set for major injury boosts ahead of Liverpool clash
item.description: Arsenal could be set for major injury boosts ahead of Liverpool clash Arsenal Injury Update Before Liverpool: Rice, Madueke and Saliba Latest Ahead of Anfield Arsenal go to Anfield with little room for self-inflicted problems. The defeat to Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup was bad enough on its own, but the bigger issue for Mikel Arteta is what it may have done to his squad depth before a major league test against Liverpool. The immediate concern is Max Dowman. He was sent off against Fleetwood, leaving Arsenal short in the wide areas at exactly the wrong moment. The club plan to appeal the straight red and hope the three-match ban is overturned in time for Sunday, but that now sits with the FA. Until there is a verdict, it remains an avoidable distraction. Declan Rice and Noni Madueke in frame There is better news elsewhere. Noni Madueke missed the Fleetwood game because of an ankle issue, but the expectation is that the injury is not serious. Arsenal are optimistic he will be available to start on the right at Anfield, which matters given the current lack of options. Declan Rice is in a similar category. He was left out entirely in midweek after feeling hamstring tightness in the second half of the win over Everton. Arsenal have handled him carefully all season and already pulled him from England duty during the last international break to manage his workload. That caution has not changed, but a full week without a midweek fixture gives him a proper chance of being ready for Liverpool. Photo IMAGO Christos Tzolis nearing return Christos Tzolis is also moving closer. He has been sidelined for nearly a month after suffering a hamstring injury on Greece duty, but his recovery has gone well. Fleetwood came too early for him, though there is a realistic possibility he makes the squad this weekend if first-team training goes smoothly over the next few days. William Saliba recovery offers Arsenal lift The longer-term update concerns William Saliba, and this is arguably the most significant one. He has not featured at all this season after Arsenal decided in the summer that a long-term back problem required a proper lay-off rather than a patch-up job. That was the sensible call. Saliba has spent the last three weeks back on the grass doing individual work and is edging towards a return to full training. If that next step passes without any setback, he could be back in an Arsenal matchday squad before the international break. So this is where Arsenal stand. Rice and Madueke are expected to have a chance, Tzolis is close, Dowman waits on an appeal, and Saliba is finally moving in the right direction. Ahead of Anfield, that counts as progress.

item.description: Rio Ngumoha heaps praise on Liverpool teammate after Chelsea win Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni show why Liverpool’s future is already arriving Liverpool’s young players took centre stage against Chelsea, and the headline was familiar. Rio Ngumoha looked sharp, direct and confident against his former club, again showing why he is viewed as one of the brightest prospects at Anfield. He drifted out of the contest in the second half, that much is true, but the damage had already been done in terms of impression. For long spells, he looked like the most dangerous attacking player on the pitch. Yet if Ngumoha grabbed the eye, Trey Nyoni may have been even better. That matters, because hype around academy talent is cheap. Production is what counts. Nyoni gave Liverpool exactly that, with a mature midfield display full of composure, volume and defensive graft. Andoni Iraola praised him afterwards, and Ngumoha was just as clear in his assessment. Trey Nyoni performance backed by numbers Nyoni’s night was built on involvement. He recorded 86 touches, more than any other player on the pitch, and attempted 76 passes. Of those, 65 found their target. The long passing still needs polishing, he completed only one of seven attempts, but the important point is that he kept looking forward. Seven passes into the final third tells its own story. This was not safe football. It was progressive football. There is also a tendency to pigeonhole young midfielders too early. Nyoni does not yet look like an out-and-out creator and he did not register a chance created in this game. Fine. Not every strong midfield display needs a highlight-reel assist attached to it. What he did offer was control, tempo and defensive reliability. He made six defensive contributions, including two tackles and four interceptions. He won three of his six ground duels and came out on top in his only aerial duel. For a 19-year-old in a high-level game, that is substance, not noise. Photo: IMAGO Rio Ngumoha praise says plenty Ngumoha did not hold back when discussing his team-mate. “Trey is top. After the NFL game in Munich on November 15 between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions, workers have only five days to replace the hybrid playing surface with grass before Bayern Munich are back in action in the Bundesliga. "We know that this will work in the short timeframe," Muth told a news conference on Thursday, acknowledging that the process will still be a "challenge." item.title: England end miserable tri-series on a high with win over Sri Lanka after Ben Duckett heroics
item.description: Ben Duckett struck a sparkling 167 off 132 balls at the Gaddafi Stadium as England finally claimed a win in their tri-series in Pakistan, beating Sri Lanka by 55 runs in a dead rubber. It was Duckett's second hundred in succession and his third in four innings in Lahore , a ground where he also made his previous ODI best. Tom Banton contributed 74 at the top of the order as England piled up 386 for five. The victory was England's first in seven ODIs in Pakistan, after they had chances to win all three previous matches and squandered seemingly unlosable positions in their last two. England had failed to defend 429 against the same opponents last Thursday, and Pavan Rathnayake's second successive century against Harry Brook's side might have brought on a case of deja vu. But Rathnayake lacked support from his middle-order colleagues. Ben Duckett hit another majestic century (PA Wire) When he sliced a sweep off Liam Dawson to depart for a majestic 118 off 77 balls, the eighth wicket to fall, the writing was on the wall. Sri Lanka were all out for 331. While their bid to simulate tournament conditions for next year's World Cup fell flat, England at least head to Australia for a white-ball series with a morale-boosting win. Sent in after losing the toss, England's openers got off to a flyer on Thursday with a 163-run stand. Banton's slash at his first delivery bounced in front of first slip, but England's openers soon got on top from the moment Duckett clipped off his legs then pulled Dilshan Madushanka for back-to-back fours in the second over. Banton was fluent off the back foot and charged slow left-armer Dunith Wellalage and part-timer Janith Liyanage for sixes down the ground. Duckett especially relied on crisp timing and methodical placement to stockpile boundaries. They each went to their fifties at better than a run-a-ball. Banton dragged Dasun Shanaka's off-cutter on to his stumps for 74, but Duckett soon brought up his sixth ODI century off just 89 deliveries. Brook promoted himself to number three and took 12 singles from his first 22 balls following his elevation. Duckett took 29 balls to go from 100 to 150 and went past his previous ODI high of 165, which came at this ground in last year's Champions Trophy, before failing to beat the short fine-leg fielder on the sweep. Will Jacks, Jordan Cox and Sam Curran were all shuffled up the order, relegating Joe Root, and they all contributed decent cameos. item.title: Skubala gives updates on Bristol City strikers ahead of Bolton
item.description: Skubala gives updates on Bristol City strikers ahead of Bolton Bristol City boss Michael Skubala has confirmed Lorent Tolaj faces a late fitness test ahead of Saturday’s trip to Bolton Wanderers. Tolaj returned to the Robins squad against Stoke City after missing the previous three games, but suffered a heavy blow to his hip following a collision with goalkeeper Viktor Johansson. “He got a big whack on Saturday,” Skubala said. “So he’s got a late fitness test for this Saturday. It’s nothing long-term, but he’s got a contusion on his hip. “He got whacked by the keeper, so it’s a massive bruise. He’s missed quite a lot of training this week, but again, it will be a late call if he makes it for Saturday.” Luke McNally is also continuing to build his fitness, but Elijah Adebayo is set to miss the next couple of games with a quad strain. “Elijah Adebayo is probably going to miss the next couple of games,” Skubala said. “We’ll see whether he makes Saturday or doesn’t make it before the next window. “He’s had a little bit of a strain; we’ve had that scanned and looked at, so he’s going to be out for the foreseeable. “He came off the pitch after Sheffield United with a quad strain. We thought he might recover quite quickly, but he’s going to need a bit more time. “I think the rest of the squad’s looking good and healthy.” There was more positive news on Rob Dickie, who has returned to training after five weeks out. “Rob’s back in, which is great news,” Skubala said. “We’ll see whether he’s available for Saturday. He’s been out five weeks, and he’s been with the team today for the first time. “We’ll see how that looks for Saturday.” Meanwhile, Noah Eile is continuing his recovery from a recent illness. “Noah’s still poorly. He’s still not available,” Skubala said. “He’s definitely heading in the right direction now,” Skubala told Bristol Live . “We’ve got a good grip of it. He’s been quite poorly, so naturally when you’re quite poorly, you lose a bit of weight and all the things you expect from being ill, but we’re definitely on the right side of it.”

item.title: Jamie Redknapp blasts 'aggressive' Mikel Arteta for public dressing down of Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman
item.description: Fleetwood Town v Arsenal - Carabao Cup Fourth Round - Getty Images Sport Jamie Redknapp has strongly criticised Mikel Arteta for his aggressive touchline reaction towards Max Dowman following the teenager's red card against Fleetwood Town. He insisted that the Arsenal manager should have waited until the dressing room to confront the young forward. Arsenal suffer shock Carabao Cup exit Arsenal suffered a shock Carabao Cup exit on Tuesday, crashing out on penalties to League Two side Fleetwood Town following a 1-1 draw . The major talking point from the match, however, was a late red card for 16-year-old Dowman . The Arsenal forward was dismissed for violent conduct in the 86th minute after kicking out at Harrison Neal. Dowman reacted in the heat of the moment after the Fleetwood midfielder caught him with a heavy challenge from behind. As Dowman left the pitch, Arteta was seen speaking sternly to the teenager on the edge of his technical area. This touchline interaction has since drawn significant criticism from former Liverpool midfielder Redknapp. Redknapp criticises aggressive touchline reaction Redknapp believes Arteta’s reaction was entirely over the top for a young player. He argued that any disciplinary discussions should always take place behind closed doors. "I don’t think you can do that," Redknapp said on The Overlap . "That has to go back in the dressing room, you have to wait. It was a very aggressive manner towards him. Just say nothing. They should have put that game to bed before 85 minutes anyway." Redknapp defends the young Arsenal forward While criticising Arteta, Redknapp showed sympathy for Dowman's sudden loss of composure. He felt that Neal was somewhat fortunate to escape punishment for the initial tackle that sparked the retaliation. "It was a dangerous tackle," Redknapp added. "In our day, you’d just go, 'What a tackle', you’d be celebrating that one. Every time you hook a player, you’re just risking hurting their knee and I suppose Dowman has just reacted." Arsenal look ahead to Liverpool clash Arsenal have launched an official appeal against Dowman’s sending off. If the red card is upheld, the teenager will serve a three-match suspension, ruling him out of Premier League fixtures against Liverpool, Hull City, and Newcastle. The club must quickly move on from one of the biggest upsets in Carabao Cup history. Arteta’s men travel to Anfield on Sunday for a massive Premier League showdown with Liverpool. Arsenal currently sit second in the league table after eight matches. They are only behind current leaders Manchester City on goal difference.

item.title: “Cooper Flagg For MVP Don’t Get It Twisted” – Mavericks Fans On Cloud Nine After ROY’s Surgical Performance Leads to Blowout Win Over Thunder
item.description: Cooper Flagg © X/ @dallasmavs Cooper Flagg’s stellar start this season continued on Wednesday as he led the Dallas Mavericks to a 120-96 win over one of the league’s best defensive units , the OKC Thunder. Flagg torched the 2025 NBA champions with a surgical offensive performance, scoring 26 points and dishing eight assists without a turnover. Flagg also grabbed five rebounds. The box score didn’t show it, but the reigning Rookie of the Year also had a solid defensive shift. After Flagg’s 26-8 game against the Thunder, his season averages improved to 25.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 6.8 assists, 2.8 steals and 1.3 blocks per game in four appearances. The numbers could have been even better had he not left Friday’s 121-105 win over the Indiana Pacers with a contact injury. In that game, Flagg had 14 points, five rebounds, six assists and three steals in just 17 minutes. As Flagg looks better with each game, Mavericks fans rallied behind him as not just an All-Star and All-NBA candidate, but also an MVP candidate. “COOPER FLAGG FOR MVP DON’T GET IT TWISTED ‼️” one fan said. Why Cooper Flagg can actually be in the conversation for MVP Whether Cooper Flagg wins MVP or not is a long shot. He’s only 19, and no one in history has achieved this milestone at that age. However, Flagg can be in that conversation. Granted, a four-game sample size is small to make such predictions, but Flagg has looked like one of the most NBA-ready prospects in recent memory. The Mavericks also developed him well in his rookie year. Former coach Jason Kidd deserves credit, as he put Flagg in uncomfortable positions and polished a few areas of his game, especially his playmaking skills as a point guard. Flagg has also gotten stronger, improving his play-finishing and ability to get to his spots. Even some of the league’s top defenders, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Aaron Nesmith and Amen Thompson, couldn’t slow him down. Flagg’s two-way versatility as a 6-foot-10 forward is rare, so he’s likely to maintain his current averages the rest of the year. If that also translates into a potential top-four finish, Flagg will have a case as an MVP candidate, as the Mavericks aren’t widely projected to make the playoffs. In terms of competition, voters might be fatigued to nominate Shai Gilgeous-Alexander for MVP for a third straight year. Luka Doncic might have the best case to win his first. Nikola Jokic’s Nuggets are off to a slow start, and he’s not been at his best either. Giannis Antetokounmpo was another MVP favorite, but after a 1-4 start, it seems Miami has a lot to figure out chemistry-wise. item.title: ‘Come on, referee’ – Ex-PGMOL chief calls out Darren England over one incident in Liverpool win
item.description: ‘Come on, referee’ – Ex-PGMOL chief calls out Darren England over one incident in Liverpool win Darren England has been criticised for not issuing a yellow card in response to one contentious incident in Liverpool’s Carabao Cup tie against Chelsea on Wednesday night. The referee booked four players over the course of the match at Anfield, but he didn’t reach for his pocket when Emmanuel Emegha inexplicably charged at Virgil van Dijk off the ball and shoved the Reds captain to the ground . The veteran defender shrugged off questions about that incident afterwards, although a former chief executive of the PGMOL (now Pro Ref) believes that the Blues striker should’ve been cautioned for his indiscetion. Hackett: England should’ve booked Emegha Speaking to Football Insider , Keith Hackett said: “Virgil van Dijk had every right to be annoyed with the referee and his opponent. The referee took no action for what was a very aggressive run and push that met the criteria for being reckless. “Van Dijk ended up on the floor, so this player is very fortunate not to receive a yellow card. Come on referee, you had a reasonable game, but you could have done better here. “This could have easily caused a mass confrontation. I am surprised and disappointed that a yellow card was not issued to the Chelsea player.” Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Emegha was lucky to avoid a yellow card Hackett is right – Emegha was fortunate to avoid a yellow card for his shove on Van Dijk, especially considering some of the bookings that England handed out earlier in the match. For example, Lewis Koumas was harshly cautioned after just 10 minutes for a minor foul on Maxence Lacroix, which was far less of an indiscretion than what the Chelsea substitute did to his fellow Dutchman in the second half. There was no discernible reason for the Blues attacker to run at the Liverpool captain and barge him to the ground, and as Hackett said, it could easily have led to a large-scale brawl between players from both teams. We don’t want to see cards being dished out unnecessarily, but Emegha’s petulance would have deserved a booking, certainly more so than Koumas for his foul on Lacroix.

item.title: Steelers’ Mike McCarthy provides encouraging injury news
item.description: Sep 27, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson (14) celebrates with wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (11) and center Zach Frazier (54) after a touchdown during the first quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium. And according to Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy, every eligible name has a chance at a return this season. “Thinking through the list, I think all those guys have a chance to come back,” McCarthy told the media Thursday. The lone exception, of course, would be defensive lineman Logan Lee, who was placed on season-ending IR before cutdown day in August. Currently, Pittsburgh’s injured reserve list features the following players: WR Roman Wilson (placed on IR Oct. 17) WR Michael Pittman Jr. (placed on IR Oct. 10) DL Derrick Harmon (placed on IR Oct. 5) DL Sebastian Joseph-Day (placed on IR Oct. 22) DL Logan Lee (placed on IR Aug. 13) OL Gennings Dunker (placed on IR Sept. 26) OL Jack Driscoll (placed on IR Aug. 30) NFL teams can bring players from IR to the 53-man roster up to eight times in the regular season per league rules. Pittsburgh has already used up two of those opportunities with safety Deshon Elliott making his Steelers return last week and Driscoll being designated to return after being placed on IR on cutdown day. However, Pittsburgh can still bring back the other five eligible names currently on the list once they miss their minimum of four games. Dunker and Driscoll could see their 21-day practice periods open at any point. Harmon and Pittman can start to return after the Steelers-Browns matchup on Nov. 1 if healthy.

item.title: Has Paige Spiranac Has Completely Changed Golf?
item.description: Aug 21, 2025; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Reporter Paige Spiranac on the first hole during the first round of the TOUR Championship golf tournament. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Paige Spiranac might not be competing on the LPGA Tour, but she’s arguably one of the most recognizable personalities in golf. Spiranac has built a massive following through social media, combining golf instruction, entertainment, and her outspoken personality to reach an audience far beyond the sport’s traditional fan base. But her popularity has also sparked criticism from those who believe golf should be more focused on competition than social media influence. Here’s the reality: Spiranac has found a way to make golf relevant to people who might otherwise never watch a tournament. Whether fans love her content or criticize her approach, there’s no denying the attention she brings to the game. item.title: Kimi Antonelli absent from Mexican Grand Prix media day ahead of F1 title coronation
item.description: Kimi Antonelli will miss media day at the Mexican Grand Prix on Thursday due to a viral illness. Antonelli needs to finish ninth or higher to guarantee the world championship this Sunday in Mexico City and, even if he finishes outside the points, George Russell or Lewis Hamilton must win the race to extend the title race to Brazil next week. Yet off the back of his impressive win in Austin last Sunday, his ninth grand prix triumph of the season, 20-year-old Antonelli is suffering from illness and has been excused from fulfilling his mandatory media duties from the FIA on Thursday. However, Mercedes do expect Antonelli to be fit and ready to go for Friday’s two practice sessions at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. A short Mercedes statement read: “Kimi is feeling under the weather today as he recovers from a viral illness. “As a precaution, the FIA have excused him from his mandatory media duties to give him the chance to rest head of the weekend. “We expect him to be back tomorrow.” Antonelli, who is set to become the sport’s youngest-ever champion, has a 123-point lead over teammate Russell with 125 points left on the table. The Italian is only in his second season in the sport, having replaced Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes last year. Only Hamilton and Jacques Villeneuve have previously won the world championship in their second season. The race on Sunday starts at 8pm GMT.

item.title: LSU’s Lane Kiffin supports 24-team College Football Playoff
item.description: The 2026 college football season is set to be the final one with the 12-team College Football Playoff. ESPN and the CFP are nearing a deal to expand to 24 teams, starting in 2027. It’s sparked mixed reactions across the college football community, and now, LSU head coach Lane Kiffin has given his take. MORE: Predicting SEC football scores in Week 9: Florida looks to keep momentum vs. Georgia In Kiffin’s mind, it “had to happen.” “I think it had to happen,” Kiffin said on the “Brandon Walker College Football Show.” “You could say, okay, 12 is better, but not when you take into account the way college football is set up now. The conferences are so different. The four conferences. They are. They’re different stadiums, they’re different environments, they’re different middle to bottom of them, and so you’re not playing equal schedules; they’re not even close. “If you took an SEC team and gave them another one of those conference’s schedules, they’d average two more wins. Well, that’s a big deal. So, I say all that to say you had to go to more teams, because the system’s broke in how they pick them, and nothing against the committee.” It should also be mentioned that an expanded playoff would help the SEC, so it’s not surprising to see Kiffin be in favor of it. His team will have an even better chance of making it to the CFP.
